questions.a: Sovereign means the people have the supreme right to decide internal and external matters and no external power can dictate to the government. A neighbour's approval of laws is such dictation. The elected rulers satisfy Democratic and the people's own constitution satisfies 'We, the People'.
o: Sovereign
Democratic
Republic
Secular

questions.q:
Two clubs in Ludhiana run sports camps. In the Ashoka Club the chair's post passes from a father to his son and nobody asks for accounts. In the Sunrise Club the members elect their chair every year, ask her for accounts, and have no official prayer, though members may pray as they like. A member of Ashoka says, 'Our post never changes hands, so the club is stable.'
(a) Whose chair is like the head of a Republic as the Preamble describes it, and why?
(b) Name two Preamble values that the Sunrise Club shows, with the reason for each.
(c) Is stability a good reason to prefer the Ashoka arrangement? Give a reasoned decision using the Preamble.
questions.a: (a) Sunrise: the head is elected and the post is not hereditary. (b) Democratic (members elect and hold her accountable) and Secular (no official religion, freedom to pray as one wishes). (c) Either side with a reason; the Preamble favours elected, accountable heads, so a strong answer notes that stability does not replace accountability, while accepting stability as a real benefit.
s: Part (a): Sunrise, elected and not hereditary
Part (b): Democratic and Secular with reasons
Part (c): a decision weighing stability against accountability with the Preamble

questions.q: A new government school lists these features: (i) admission is open to children of every caste, religion and gender; (ii) there is no official prayer and students keep their own festivals without asking permission; (iii) the students' council is elected each year and must present its accounts to the students; (iv) students are told they may not write or speak on any rule of the school, even politely; (v) boys and girls get the same chance to enter every competition. Name the Preamble value reflected in (i), (ii), (iii) and (v) with a reason, and say which feature goes against a Preamble value, which one, and what change you would suggest.
questions.a: (i) Justice: no discrimination on caste, religion or gender. (ii) Secular: no official religion and freedom to follow any faith. (iii) Democratic: rulers are elected and held accountable. (v) Equality: equal opportunity for all. (iv) goes against Liberty: there should be no unreasonable restrictions on how citizens express their thoughts; students should be allowed to put forward views on school rules politely.
s: Justice for (i) with reason
Secular for (ii) with reason
Democratic for (iii) with reason
Equality for (v) with reason
(iv) against Liberty with a suggested change

questions.q: A government announces: 'We will treat all religions with equal respect, and from next year one religion will be the official religion of the State.' Using the Preamble's meaning of Secular, show why the two parts of the announcement cannot both hold.
questions.a: Secular means citizens have complete freedom to follow any religion, but there is no official religion, and the government treats all beliefs and practices with equal respect. Naming one religion the official religion of the State breaks the 'no official religion' part and therefore the 'equal respect' part too, so the two promises contradict each other.
s: States the chapter's meaning: no official religion, equal respect
Shows an official religion contradicts equal respect
Concludes the two cannot both be true

questions.q:
Match each situation (Column A) with the Preamble word it shows (Column B).

questions.a: No official religion with freedom of practice is Secular; regulating ownership of land and industry is Socialist; no discrimination on caste or gender is Justice; refusing outside dictation is Sovereign.

Assertion (A): Under 'Secular', the Government of India has an official religion but allows other faiths to be practised.
Reason (R): Under 'Secular', citizens have complete freedom to follow any religion.

questions.q: Why does the Preamble begin with 'We, the People of India' and not with the name of a ruler? (a) Give the reason the chapter states. (b) Which Preamble word then tells us who holds the supreme right to take decisions for the country?
questions.a: (a) The Constitution was drawn up and enacted by the people through their representatives, and was not handed down by a king or any outside power. (b) Sovereign: the people have the supreme right to make decisions on internal as well as external matters.
s: Part (a): drawn up by the people through representatives, not handed down
Part (b): Sovereign, with the people holding supreme right

questions.q:
Read the statements about the Preamble.
1. In a Republic, the head of state is chosen by the previous head of state, which keeps the position out of any one family.
2. 'Secular' means the State treats every religion with equal respect, so it must encourage every citizen to follow a religion.
3. 'Socialist' means wealth is generated socially and should be shared, and the government should regulate the ownership of land and industry to reduce socio-economic inequalities.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: Only statement 3 is from the chapter. Statement 1 is false: a Republic's head of state is an elected person. Statement 2 is false: Secular means complete freedom to follow any religion, with no official religion; it does not require anyone to follow one.
o: 3 only
1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only

questions.q: Analyse how the words 'Sovereign', 'Democratic' and 'Republic' together describe the way India is governed.
questions.a: Sovereign: the people decide internal and external matters and no external power can dictate. Democratic: the people elect their rulers, hold them accountable and the government follows basic rules. Republic: the head of the state is elected, not hereditary. Together they show a country whose government is controlled by its own people, chosen by them and answerable to them.
s: Sovereign explained
Democratic explained
Republic explained
Links the three to rule by the people, chosen and answerable

questions.q: Name the Preamble value shown in each, with a reason: (i) Meera and Zoya, of different faiths, share their lunch and neither thinks the other inferior; (ii) a sarpanch must explain to the villagers how the funds were spent; (iii) every applicant to a school sits the same entrance test irrespective of caste or gender.
questions.a: (i) Fraternity: they behave as members of one family and no one is treated as inferior. (ii) Democratic: rulers are held accountable by the people. (iii) Equality or Justice: no discrimination and equal opportunity.
s: (i) Fraternity with reason
(ii) Democratic with reason
(iii) Equality or Justice with reason

questions.q: Tara says, 'The Preamble says Socialist, so the government must take over all land and industry and no one may own any.' Test her claim against the chapter.
questions.a: No. The chapter explains Socialist as wealth being generated socially and shared by society, and says the government should regulate the ownership of land and industry to reduce socio-economic inequalities. Regulating ownership is not the same as abolishing it, and the chapter does not say that no one may own anything.
s: Verdict: disagrees
States the chapter's meaning of Socialist
Regulate versus take over or abolish

questions.q: In a town, the mayor is chosen each year by a lottery among the town's families, and she need not explain her spending to anyone. Which idea in the Preamble's description of 'Democratic' is missing?
questions.a: Democratic means the people enjoy equal political rights, elect their rulers and hold them accountable. A lottery means the people do not elect the ruler, and the mayor does not answer to the people, so the central ideas of electing rulers and holding them accountable are both absent.
o: The people elect their rulers and hold them accountable
The head of state is an elected person and not a hereditary one
No external power can dictate to the government
There is no official religion and every faith is treated with equal respect

questions.q: Which of these situations fails the Preamble's meaning of Equality, as the chapter explains it?
questions.a: Equality means all are equal before the law and the government should ensure equal opportunity for all. A hospital that serves a patient only after learning her caste denies that equality; the other situations give everyone the same law or the same chance.
o: A hospital serves a patient only after learning her caste
A minister and a labourer are tried under the same law
Every applicant sits the same entrance test
A scholarship notice invites applications from everyone eligible
